title: Martyrs and Witnesses
lead: The Greek martys means "witness," someone who testifies in court, and in the early church it came to mean a witness who died for the faith. The Bible's line of faithful people killed for God runs from Abel (Genesis 4:10; Matthew 23:35) through the prophets (1 Kings 19:10; 2 Chronicles 24:20–22) and the Maccabean martyrs (2 Maccabees 6–7) to Stephen (Acts 7:54–60), James (Acts 12:2) and the souls under the altar in Revelation (Revelation 6:9–11).
